claims: scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:759: `classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal` only returns `reviewed` when it finds a PR review with a `**Run ID**` in the body, but a clean CodeRabbit run appears to post only a walkthrough issue comment, so a clean run probably never reaches `reviewed` (reads `missing` or `stale`)
Same incorrect claim about clean-run detection appears in docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:111-114 and .claude/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:296 (plus its .agents mirror)

Consequence of the clean-run misclassification: the new closeout rule posts `@coderabbitai review` on an already-reviewed head, wasting hourly review quota, and the gate then sits at `requested` forever

docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:399-402: the runbook puts the request step in the wrong place; new step 8 comes after the final pair (step 5) and acting on ready-state (step 7), contradicting pr-operating-card.md:157, babysit SKILL.md:295 and ship SKILL.md:215, so CodeRabbit findings can land after all-clear
docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:276-305: the sample JSON is out of date; it lacks `gates.codeRabbitReviewSignal` and the top-level `codeRabbitReviewSignal` described in the field list

No CodeRabbit check at all: with `.coderabbit.yaml` `base_branches: []` and `drafts: false`, stacked (and maybe paused) PRs may have no check, and none of the four docs says whether to wait or request right away

Quota: raising the pause threshold from 2 to 5 and adding a request per stale head both use more reviews against the Pro+ limit of 4 per hour, and the ADR gives no numbers to support that it 'spends the ladder on review rounds that matter'
The 16/29 and 6-PR sample figures in the ADR are unverified
coderabbit-config.test.mjs:124: the renamed config test only compares the pinned constant against itself

judge_reasoning.3829654081: The review never raises the file's line count or asks for pr-ready-state-core.mjs to be split.
judge_reasoning.3829659544: Finding 3 says the sample JSON in pr-ready-state.md lacks gates.codeRabbitReviewSignal and the top-level field.
judge_reasoning.3829659546: Finding 2 says the runbook puts the CodeRabbit request step after the final feedback/ready-state pair, unlike the other docs, and should move it before the final invocation.
judge_reasoning.3829659550: The review never discusses currentHeadOid being null and the fallback to timestamps or any marker; it only says the marker is tied to the full head SHA.

1.why: At core.mjs:759-770, `reviewed` needs a coderabbitai review whose body has `**Run ID**`. The repo's fixture of a real PR (#1918, feedback-state.test.mjs:3360-3373) shows 'No actionable comments were generated in the recent review. 🎉' inside the walkthrough issue comment, which the classifier never reads, so a clean run ends up `missing` or `stale`.

2.why: pr-ready-state.md:111-114, .claude/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:296 (the .agents copy is byte-identical per diff) and cloud-watch-loop.md:49 all say a Run ID review body is required for `reviewed`. They repeat the clean-run gap from claim 1.

3.why: This follows from claim 1. A clean head reads `missing`/`stale`, so the fallbackAction (core.mjs ~1012) says to post `@coderabbitai review`. Once the marker is posted the state is `requested`, and it can only move to `reviewed` through a Run ID review that a clean run never creates.

4.why: Checked: pr-ready-state.md step 8 comes after the final pair (step 5) and step 7, which contradicts operating-card:157, babysit SKILL:295 and ship SKILL:215 ('before the final pair'). It restates the known pr-ready-state.md:408 Major finding about all-clear (steps 8-10).

5.why: The sample JSON at pr-ready-state.md:276-305 has gates.codexReviewSignal and top-level codexReviewSignal but no codeRabbitReviewSignal. The new field list (351-355) and the code (core.mjs gates plus the return object) do include it.

6.why: base_branches: [] and drafts: false are in .coderabbit.yaml, but the claim only says a check 'may' be missing. I can't confirm from the repo whether CodeRabbit posts a check on skipped PRs, and no concrete failure is shown.

7.why: This criticises the quota trade-off and the ADR's wording. It names no concrete defect in the code or config.

8.why: The 16/29 and six-PR figures are cited GitHub query results in the ADR evidence section. 'Unverified' names no defect I can check in the repo.

9.why: coderabbit-config.test.mjs:121-125 asserts EXPECTED_CONFIG's value equals the literal 5, not the constant against itself. The real YAML is already pinned by the deepEqual test at line ~101, so coverage has no gap; at most the test is redundant.
